item.text:
1. Placed CURVE DATA tables in paper space on C-101 (curve 1), C-102 (curves 1 and 2), and C-103 (curve 2), with No., R, Δ, T and L columns. Added circled-number leader callouts aimed at curve 1 on C-102 and curve 2 on C-103. The curve extents cross the sheet boundaries, so each curve appears on both sheets it spans.

2. Tool calls that mattered, in order:
   - `get_document_state({})`; `list_references({})`; `list_alignments({include_references:true})`
   - `get_design_data({alignment:"DESIGN:SR-100", kind:"curves"})` to identify curve data and stations
   - `get_sheet_state({sheet:"C-101"|"C-102"|"C-103"})` to check viewports
   - `place_curve_table` on each sheet with the referenced alignment and curve indices `[1]`, `[1,2]`, `[2]`, respectively; columns `["curve","radius","delta","tangent","length"]`
   - `place_callout` with `target_anchor:"MC-1"` on C-102 and `target_anchor:"MC-2"` on C-103, using circled numbers `①` and `②`

3. Two callouts failed because the target was outside the selected sheet’s viewport:
   - C-101: “DESIGN:SR-100 MC-1 at 25+98.32 (2597.49, 1015.50) is not visible through any viewport of C-101”
   - C-102: “DESIGN:SR-100 MC-2 at 41+76.51 (4101.89, 1488.38) is not visible through any viewport of C-102”
   
   The engine indicated those locations were visible on C-102 and C-103, respectively, so I placed the callouts there.
